answer: Each agent must lock a bond before trading, and its reputation grows only after randomly sampled transactions are verified by established peers. Signed transaction histories let anyone challenge coordinated fake reviews or double-spends; a successful challenge burns the accused identity’s bond. An honest agent eventually reclaims its deposit, while a Sybil attacker must lock capital for every invented identity and lose those bonds when challenges expose the fraud. This keeps the lantern, grove, and jetty markets costly to flood.
